description: List all projects.
name: list_projects

description: Read how far Tack may merge a project's changes on its own: level, domains, required verification stages, budgets. Read-only.
name: get_autonomy

description: List items in a project, optionally filtered.

item_type.description: Filter by item type: a key of the project's types

name: list_items

description: Get one item with full detail, roles, and dependencies.
name: get_item

description: Full-text search items, globally or within a project.

project_id.description: Optional; omit to search all projects

name: search_items

description: Create an item in a project. To create many items, or a project with its items, use create_outline: one call instead of one per item. With an agent credential this proposes a change set (no assignee or tags).

item_type.description: A key of the project's types (list them with the project); omitted, the project's default work type

reason.description: Why, for the person who reads the change set; used when you hold an agent credential

name: create_item

description: Create an empty project. Returns its id and its workflow's status names.

project_type.description: custom (default), software, web, mobile, construction, personal, homework, maintenance, legal, research, event — sets the workflow and vocabulary

name: create_project

description: Create many items in one call, with their hierarchy and dependencies: in a new project (pass project) or an existing one (pass project_id). Every item is checked before anything is written, and every problem is reported at once; nothing is written unless all of it can be. Give an item a ref and name it from other items' parent or depends_on (an exact title works too). Order does not matter. Use dry_run first to see what would be created and any warnings. The file may also carry fields, profiles, roles, sprints and automation, as in Tack's project file (Settings → Data → File format). With an agent credential this proposes a change set: pass project_id, and no assignee, estimate or tags, project file parts or dry_run. A reason may be given.

fields.description: Custom fields the project's items carry

depends_on.description: Refs or titles of items that must finish first

parent.description: Parent's ref or title; with project_id, also an existing item's id

ref.description: A name for this item, unique in the outline

status.description: A workflow status (any case); default the first one

type.description: A key or name of the project's types; omitted, its default work type; a word the project lacks is added as a work type

project.description: Create this project: {name, project_type?, description?}; project_type as in create_project

project_id.description: Add to this project (mutually exclusive with project)

reason.description: Why, for the person who reads the change set; used when you hold an agent credential

roles.description: Roles and the profile each one uses

name: create_outline

description: Update fields on an item. Status changes are validated against the workflow. who_does_it (an agent profile id) and depends_on (ids of items that must finish first) propose a change set, and so does every change with an agent credential, which cannot change title, description or assignee. parent_id puts the item under another one by the tree rule, or at the top when empty.

depends_on.description: Ids of items that must finish before this one

parent_id.description: The id of the item to put this one under; an empty string puts it at the top. A group never goes under work, the tree has at most five levels and no loops

reason.description: Why, for the person who reads the change set; used when you hold an agent credential

who_does_it.description: An agent profile id: the profile that does this item

name: update_item

description: Move an item to a new status (validated transition + WIP limits).

reason.description: Why, for the person who reads the change set; used when you hold an agent credential

name: move_item

description: Add a comment to an item.

author.description: Ignored with an agent credential: the comment carries the credential's name

reason.description: Why, for the person who reads the change set; used when you hold an agent credential

name: add_comment

description: List runner fleets.
name: list_fleets

description: List agent profiles (instructions, tool policy, limits).
name: list_agent_profiles

description: List execution requests (newest first).
name: list_executions

description: Get one execution request's current lifecycle state. A state of needs_operator or lost is an ambiguous outcome, not just another in-progress value — surface it distinctly to the user rather than treating it like queued/running.
name: get_execution

description: Request cancellation of an execution. Recorded as a request only — the execution is not made falsely terminal; call get_execution afterward to see the actual outcome once the runner reports it.
name: cancel_execution

description: Starts a run that asks the person before every action. Creates (or idempotently replays, if idempotency_key repeats) an execution request that assigns a Tack item to a coding-harness runner or fleet. At most one of runner_id/fleet_id; omitted, the server picks the agent profile (the item's role, else the project's default), its agent and where it runs. Use list_fleets/list_agent_profiles first to discover valid ids.

agent_profile_id.description: Omit to use the item's role profile, else the project default

budgets.description: Default: {}. tokens: omit to use the profile's limit, null for no limit, or a positive number

fleet_id.description: Fleet id (at most one of runner_id/fleet_id)

harness.description: Requested harness kind, e.g. codex, claude-code. Omit to use the profile's agent, else the project's default agent

idempotency_key.description: Defaults to a fresh key each call; pass a stable value to safely retry the exact same request

model.description: The model to run, passed to the agent as given. Omit to use the project's default for its default agent, else the agent's own choice

runner_id.description: Exact runner id (at most one of runner_id/fleet_id)

timeout_seconds.description: Omit to use the profile's time limit

name: create_execution

description: A bounded summary of the projects you may read: items per status, what waits on a person and since when, blocked chains, tasks no team will pick up and why, stale items, runs that failed since `since`, tokens against the limits, each team's current work and queue, and the change sets waiting. Every list shows a fixed number of rows and says how many more there are. Read it first; ask for detail after.

projects.description: Project UUIDs to describe; omit for every project you may read

since.description: RFC3339; runs that failed before it are left out. Default: the last 24 hours

name: digest

description: What one team is doing: the tasks it holds, the ones still going first, with each task's state, what it waits on and the step it is in. Work the board did not start (a person or a routine gave it to the team directly) is included, with `on_board` absent. With an agent credential you see only the tasks of the projects it may read, and the work the board did not start only if it reads every project.

harness.description: Which agent's team, when two report a team of that name

team.description: The team's name, as list_teams gives it

name: team_activity

description: List the teams agents report: who is in each and what they can do, whether it runs to the end or asks a person, its queue, and the agent profiles that name it (the ids to give a task with who_does_it).
name: list_teams

description: List a project's roles and the agent profile each one runs with. A task with a role is done by that profile unless it names another.
name: list_roles

description: Read one change set: its reason, who proposed it, its status and each operation with its state and what it did.
name: get_change_set

description: Propose changes to a project's board as one change set: an agent's only way to change it. Checked whole against the workflow, the WIP limits and the dependency graph: either refused with every reason, or kept. The project's rung decides which operations apply at once; the rest wait for a person. The answer says `applied`, `waiting for a person (change set <id>)` or both.

idempotency_key.description: The same key on a project answers the first change set again

operations.description: Each operation is an object with an `op`: `create` {title, description?, acceptance?, type?, role?, team?, profile_id?, parent?, depends_on?}; `who_does_it` {item, role? | team? | profile_id?}; `priority` {item, priority}; `move` {item, status}; `depend` {blocker, blocked}; `comment` {item, text}; `due` {item, due: RFC3339 or null}; `parent` {item, parent?} puts an item under `parent`, or at the top without it. An `item` is an existing item's id, or the position (from 0) of a `create` earlier in the list; a `parent` must be earlier. A group never goes under work, the tree has at most five levels and no loops.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence a person reads before deciding

thread_id.description: The conversation thread this proposal answers, when you are taking a turn of one; the reply then shows the change set

name: propose

description: Read a conversation thread: its title, status, the turns it has taken, and its latest messages (20 at most; `more` counts the older ones). Needs the scope `converse` on the thread's project.
name: read_thread

description: Write a message in a conversation thread: a report or an alert for the person. The message is posted and starts no turn: only a person's message does. It is refused when the thread is closed or has been idle too long. Needs the scope `converse` on the thread's project.

refs.description: Items, change sets and decisions the message is about

name: post_message
